title: 门槛
status: 焦土迷宫入口概念图，首轮画风评审
prompt:
Paint ONE finished horizontal 16:10 concept illustration for an original fictional game, titled in the brief “Threshold” (do not print any title). It is one uninterrupted scene: an exhausted traveler with no provisions, a living human gatekeeper seated at his little trading-card stall, and the entrance to an immense UNKNOWN labyrinth in the same scorched ash plain. This image is specifically for judging the illustrated art style and the relationship between those two people.

ART DIRECTION: Make it immediately and confidently a stylized 2D PAINTING. An opaque, limited-palette gouache and softly overlapped cut-paper sensibility. Organize people, drapery and architecture into a few well-designed, quiet shapes. Faces have just a light plane, a shadow plane and one eyelid accent. Model sleeves with two decisive brush shapes. Silhouette edges are defined by adjacent different-value colors, broken or lost in shadows; there are absolutely no black contour lines or ink outlines around forms, no hatching. An occasional pigment scumble at an edge and barely-there paper tooth; much of every wall and patch of sky is a continuous field of color. Adult, spare, emotionally rich game illustration. Neither photorealism nor cutesy cartoon nor technical 3D rendering. No pores, crisp textile weave, tiny decorative scratches, or uniform digital grain.

COMPOSITION: Shoulder-height view from a few paces out on the threshold, looking obliquely across a slight ash slope. In the left third, an adult survivor in a close-fitting short dusty ochre jacket stands in three-quarter profile facing right. Leaning gently forward, one foot has stopped where gritty ash meets a swept, worn sill. The survivor is a substantial full-length shape, about 45 percent of image height. Their lowered hand has just tipped an unmistakably limp, collapsed provision pouch upside down; a tiny pinch of ash falls from its opening. Keep a little negative space below the elbow so that the empty pouch reads. No warrior pose. In the right-middle foreground a middle-aged human gatekeeper sits low and heavily behind a knee-high simple trestle table, face, hands and tabletop easy to see, his posture angled toward the open maze. Broad hanging sleeves, one oversized falling cuff, lowered eyelids, slightly absent expression; bare head, no armor or wizard regalia. His dark clothes and table edges carry dust. On the otherwise bare stall he has laid out a small square of meticulously tended cloth and three separate warm, pale, hand-size, rounded paper trading cards. We can see their faces with simple faded abstract overlapping doorway motifs. Two fingers of his near hand carefully flatten the skewed corner of one card; he holds the opposite edge of the cloth steady with the other. A partly screened tiny lamp catches just his fingertips and the cards. The stall, the empty pouch and his reverent gesture must be legible on first viewing. The figures share a grounded plane, in believable scale with each other.

Behind and between them two vast off-register vertical masses of soot-violet earthen stone form the unmistakable entrance. Their tops are deliberately cropped beyond the top edge, one sunken plane turns away behind the next. A thin cool reflection on a single worn step just inside makes it clear one can physically walk in, then the path bends out of view immediately. In the far left, ash-colored distant slope and a breath of dusty sky; no village. Compose the broad wall masses first, then lead the eye down a diagonal fold of the keeper’s sleeve to the small light rectangle of paper. Limited colors: charcoal violet #35323D, dusty blue grey #727986, earthen muted ochre #9A7C69, aged paper cream #E1D3B4, a restrained ember-orange note #CA9164 only near the lamp. Leave the rest of the light cool, enough separation to see both human silhouettes. Allow asymmetry, silence and large undetailed spaces. No letterforms, numbers, HUD, captions, border, split panels, symbols in the sky, weapons, rust piles, torches, robots or magical spectacle.
